Kitchener joined our entire community and those in Toronto and beyond in extending our
sincere sympathies to the family and friends of former Mayor Morley Rosenberg.
Serving as Kitchener's 53rd Mayor from 1977 to 1982, Mayor Rosenberg first served as the
City of Kitchener Alderman, as they were called back in the day, from 1968 to 1976, and also
served on the Council of the Regional Municipality of Waterloo.
At 87 years of age at the time of his passing, Morley Rosenberg, a lawyer by training, lived
a life committed to public service.
During his tenure at the City of Kitchener, he fought to preserve Kitchener's historic
City Hall, was a strong proponent for engagement with community groups, and pushed for the
creation of the ward system that still serves Kitchener residents to this very day.
The preservation of the clock tower from that historic City Hall saw it permanently eventually
placed in Victoria Park in 1995 and being included on the City logo used today.
Mayor Rosenberg was also mayor when the Centre in the Square opened in 1980 and to this day
that facility remains one of the best performing arts centres of its size in the country from
an acoustic perspective.
Mayor Rosenberg was also a strong advocate for recycling, serving as mayor in the years
when the City worked with community members and the private sector to introduce the Blue
box program to Canada and the world.
Subsequent to his time at the City, former Mayor Rosenberg served Ontario residents on
the Ontario Municipal Board for 20 years.
Moving to Toronto many years back, Morley's commitment to public service continued even
after his time with the OMB, including serving on the City of Toronto's Committee of Adjustment,
working with community groups on planning matters, and even seeking a seat on Toronto
Council in 2018 at the age of 81.
